draft.title: Missing derivatives of a thin singular value decomposition
draft.body:
## Reproducer

Run this example

```sh
cat > thin-svd.mlir <<'MLIR'
func.func @vals(%a: tensor<4x3xf32>) -> tensor<3xf32> {
  %r:4 = enzymexla.linalg.svd %a : (tensor<4x3xf32>) -> (tensor<4x3xf32>, tensor<3xf32>, tensor<3x3xf32>, tensor<i32>)
  return %r#1 : tensor<3xf32>
}
MLIR
enzymexlamlir-opt thin-svd.mlir --enzyme-wrap='infn=vals outfn= retTys=enzyme_active argTys=enzyme_active mode=ReverseModeCombined'
```

## Observed

The upstream base used by the stack has no adjoint for the SVD operation.

## Expected

For distinct, nonzero singular values and output cotangent g, the real input adjoint should be U diag(g) Vᵀ.

## Proposed fix

Define forward and reverse rules for the thin SVD, reusing the primal factors and handling rectangular shapes. Phase-dependent complex objectives need separate treatment. The upstream reverse proposal is [#2551](https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme-JAX/pull/2551); the fork rules were described in [#3277](https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Enzyme-JAX/pull/3277).

problems.title: An unused generated operand prevents the triangular-solve rules from compiling with strict warnings
problems.summary: The helper that forms the triangular-solve outer product accepts a matrix operand it never reads. Both generated derivative implementations declare an unused mlir::Value. Clang rejects the generated code when unused-variable warnings are errors.

commits.title: Drop the unused operand of the triangular_solve outer-product subroutines

draft.title: Triangular-solve derivatives generate an unused local under Clang
draft.body: Build the XLADerivatives target with Clang 21 and -Werror=unused-variable after #3948. The generated MHLO and StableHLO implementations declare an unused mlir::Value for the matrix operand in TriangularSolveDiffOuterRaw. Removing that operand from the two TableGen subroutines and their call sites lets both implementations compile.

problems.title: Reverse differentiation needs a static trip bound for a data-dependent while loop
problems.summary: The forward pass counts actual iterations of a replayable stablehlo.while. Reverse mode uses binomial checkpointing with 32 carry snapshots by default. The body and its callees must be free of memory effects, and the carried tensors must have static shapes. The checkpoint period selects the snapshot budget. Explicitly disabling checkpointing retains the bounded tape path.

commits.title: Reverse-differentiate stablehlo.while loops whose trip count is data-dependent

draft.title: Reverse-differentiate a replayable stablehlo.while with a data-dependent trip count
draft.body: A convergence test in an adaptive integrator can make the trip count unknowable until the forward run finishes. Without a static bound, reverse differentiation fails during cache removal. With a large bound it can allocate a correspondingly large tape. The regression in test/lit_tests/diffrules/stablehlo/while_data_dependent_trip_count.mlir checks gradients for zero trips, nested loops and several snapshot budgets. A second fixture checks that replay preserves the behavior of callbacks.

problems.title: Reverse mode can run too few iterations of a while loop
problems.summary: When the reverse pass undercounts loop iterations, it drops gradient contributions. Floating-point counters need the number of trips actually taken. For an increasing integer counter, the last partial stride contributes one trip, and a loop that never enters contributes zero.

commits.title: WhileLoopInfo: count only integer loops, round a runtime trip count up

draft.title: Reverse differentiation undercounts some StableHLO while loops
draft.body: Start a floating-point accumulator at zero and repeatedly add a = 0.5 while it is below 2.4. The forward loop executes five additions. At that input its derivative with respect to a should be 5, but reverse mode returns 4. Integer loops also lose the last iteration when a runtime bound is between strides. For example, a loop starting at zero with step 2 and bound 5 visits 0, 2 and 4. The derivative of an accumulator that adds a once per trip should be 3. The regression also covers an empty interval and a floating-point counter whose repeated additions round.
